classes.name: Metformin (biguanide)
classes.description: Biguanide oral therapy (metformin IR/ER) — guideline first-line pharmacotherapy for type 2 diabetes.
classes.plainDescription: The standard first pill for type 2 diabetes. Cheap, effective, decades of use.

classes.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
classes.description: GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, dulaglutide, liraglutide) and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide — for type 2 diabetes with weight and cardiovascular benefit.
classes.plainDescription: Injectable (usually weekly) diabetes medicines that also help with weight. Most plans require approval first.

classes.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
classes.description: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin) — oral therapy with heart-failure and kidney benefit.
classes.plainDescription: A once-a-day pill that lowers blood sugar and protects the heart and kidneys.
classes.indication: Type 2 diabetes; heart failure & CKD benefit

records.verificationNote: Read page 44 (OZEMPIC pen, Tier 3, PA, QL 3 per 28 days) and page 43 (MOUNJARO pen, Tier 3, PA, QL 2 per 28 days). Both products are diabetes-labeled. Every covered GLP-1 on the list needs PA, so the lowest-barrier pick is Ozempic (same tier, same restriction) and the barrier is stated in preferredRestriction. Trulicity, Victoza/liraglutide, Rybelsus, Byetta and Bydureon are not on the list; the document does not say the list is complete, so they are not recorded as excluded. Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda do not appear on the list; weight-loss products are not recorded as covered or excluded. Partial because absent GLP-1 products cannot be confirmed as non-covered from this document. Sig is standard label dosing.

records.verificationNote: Read page 42: dapagliflozin 5 and 10 mg tablet (generic), Tier 3, QL 30 per 30 days, no PA/ST; FARXIGA on the same page is Tier 3 with the same QL. Page 43: JARDIANCE 10 and 25 mg Tier 3 with the same QL. The document does not indicate a brand preference between the generic and FARXIGA, so boglActive false. Canagliflozin and generic empagliflozin do not appear on the list. Sig is standard label dosing.

records.verificationNote: Read pages 43 and 44: LANTUS SoloStar U-100 pen and vial, Tier 3, CI and MO, no PA/ST. Page 10 defines CI as Part D covered insulin products. LANTUS was picked as the basal preferred agent because it is the most-prescribed basal product of the covered basal lines; no generic glargine is on the list, so boglActive false. Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar, Humalog, Admelog and Lyumjev do not appear on the list. The document does not state the list is complete, so these are not recorded as excluded; partial because the preferred basal pick could differ if one of them is covered. Humulin R U-500 (page 43, Tier 5, DL) is a concentrated regular insulin and excluded from the basal alternatives. Soliqua (page 44) is a glargine-lixisenatide combination and excluded.
